title: The fibrewise local-complete-intersection locus is open and base-change compatible
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Put $s=f(x)$ for $x\in X$, and let $X_s$ denote its scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $V_f$ be the set of $x$ such that $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $\kappa(s)$, with the local-ring meaning in [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion]. For every morphism $S'\to S$, write $f':X'=X\times_SS'\to S'$ and $g':X'\to X$ for the base change and projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $V_{f'}=(g')^{-1}(V_f)$. If $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], then $V_f$ is open. This open is the syntomic locus: it is the largest source open whose restriction is flat, locally of finite presentation, and has local-complete-intersection fibres, where that fibre condition means that every local ring of every fibre is a complete-intersection local ring over its residue base field. Empty fibres and the empty source are allowed.

source.place: Tag 02V3 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-lci), including its last assertion on the open syntomic locus and its fibre-local-ring definition of the locus.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ over $s\in S$. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], choose affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ about $s$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$ about $x$, mapping into $\operatorname{Spec}A$, with $B$ finitely generated over $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], this chart cuts out an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $X_s$, with $C=B\otimes_A k$ and $k=\kappa(s)$. If $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ generate $B$ over $A$, then $b_1\otimes1,\ldots,b_r\otimes1$ generate $C$ over $k$: expand each element as a finite sum of tensors and then expand its $B$-factor as a polynomial in the $b_i$. Thus $C$ is a finite type $k$-algebra. This construction for all points gives a locally finite type fibre, without assuming $f$ flat or locally finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 02V3 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-lci), first part, affine form of the locally finite type hypothesis.

proof.text: Fix any $x'\in X'$, put $s'=f'(x')$, $x=g'(x')$, $s=f(x)$, $k=\kappa(s)$ and $K=\kappa(s')$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change], $X'_{s'}=X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$, compatibly with the projections to $X$. Take the finite type affine chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}C\subset X_s$ of step 1 around $x$. Its inverse image is an open neighbourhood of $x'$, by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], and equals $\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_k C)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and the tensor interchange $c\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes c$. The prime $\mathfrak q_K$ of this chart representing $x'$ contracts to the prime $\mathfrak q$ representing $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the two fibre local rings are $C_{\mathfrak q}$ and $(K\otimes_k C)_{\mathfrak q_K}$. Apply [lem-trf-lci-field-change-local]: the first is a complete intersection over $k$ exactly when the second is one over $K$. Hence $x'\in V_{f'}$ if and only if $g'(x')\in V_f$. Since $x'$ was arbitrary this proves the asserted equality of subsets.

source.place: Tag 02V3 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-lci), first paragraph of proof, applying Algebra Tag 00SI (lemma-lci-field-change-local).

proof.text: Now assume $f$ flat and locally of finite presentation, and take $x\in V_f$, with $s=f(x)$. By [def-weil-flat-morphism] the local map at $x$ is flat, and by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] $f$ is of finite presentation at $x$. Membership in $V_f$ is exactly the remaining complete-intersection local-fibre hypothesis of [lem-trf-syntomic-pointwise-local-model]. For an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ about $s$, apply that lemma to get an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ about $x$, mapping into $V$, and a relative-global-complete-intersection presentation $B=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$.

source.place: Tag 02V3 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-lci), second paragraph of proof; Tag 01UE (lemma-syntomic-locally-standard-syntomic), implication (3) to (2).

proof.text: For each $t\in V$, the fibre of $U\to V$ is $\operatorname{Spec}D_t$, where $D_t=B\otimes_R\kappa(t)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. By [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change], it has the presentation $D_t=\kappa(t)[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(\overline h_1,\ldots,\overline h_c)$. By [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection], either $D_t=0$ or $\dim D_t=n-c$. In either case $D_t$ is a global complete intersection over $\kappa(t)$ by [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field], hence a local complete intersection (the single principal open $D(1)$ covers its spectrum). By [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion], every local ring of $\operatorname{Spec}D_t$ is a complete-intersection local ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], this fibre is the open subspace $U\cap X_t$ of $X_t$; its local ring at any of its points is unchanged, since a germ can be represented on a neighbourhood inside that open. Thus every $y\in U$ belongs to $V_f$. Each $x\in V_f$ has such an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq V_f$, so $V_f$ is their union and is open.

source.place: Tag 02V3 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-lci), last assertion; Tag 01UE (lemma-syntomic-locally-standard-syntomic), affine local model.

proof.text: For any source open $H\subseteq X$, [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] identifies its fibre at $s$ with $H\cap X_s$. Its local rings are the same as those of $X_s$ at its points, by the germ argument in step 4. Therefore every fibre local ring of $H\to S$ is a complete intersection exactly when $H\subseteq V_f$. Flatness restricts to $H$ because the source local rings and their maps are unchanged, using [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Local finite presentation restricts as well: inside a witnessing affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], choose a principal neighbourhood $D(b)$ of the point contained in $H$; if $B=R[\mathbf t]/(\mathbf h)$, its algebra is $B_b=R[\mathbf t,u]/(\mathbf h,bu-1)$, still finitely presented. Apply this to $H=V_f$ to obtain all three stated properties of its restriction. Conversely any source open having those properties is contained in $V_f$ by its fibre condition. This proves maximality, the stated description of the syntomic locus, and includes the empty source and empty fibres (there are then no points or local rings to check).

source.place: Tag 02V3 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-lci), last assertion, with the source-open description expanded from the definitions.
